description: GAP-2 closure (AG32-Docs docs/TASK_QUEUE.md queue B, task B3; the 'from-source Rule 2' named in AG32-Docs docs/PROMOTION_TIER_AMENDMENT_PROPOSAL.md as T9). qualification/pack_regression.json's routed_sha256 only detects tampering of an already-retained, already-routed JSON file: it re-PACKS a pinned netlist and never asks nextpnr to choose a route again, so it is structurally blind to nextpnr picking a DIFFERENT route for unchanged source under a grown/changed chipdb -- the exact 2026-08-18 failure mode (T26/A1b) where mcu_ahb_constant_slave's fresh route drifted onto the open X14Y8 RMUX->IMUX->RMUX detour with the design's own cap=2 seed=4 unchanged. This file pins, per designated design, the ROUTE hash (not just the bitstream hash) a genuine fresh synth+place+route is expected to reproduce. 'Route hash' uses exactly pack_regression.json's canonicalization: strip CRLF to LF, sha256 the resulting bytes of the nextpnr --write JSON (see tests/test_qualified_pack_regression.py's _canonical_lf and tests/test_route_from_source_invariance.py's identical helper). Exercised only by tests/test_route_from_source_invariance.py, gated behind AGAMEMNON_TEST_FROM_SOURCE_ROUTE=1 and a real yosys+nextpnr-generic toolchain, because a real synth+route build is minutes per design, not milliseconds -- this must never run in the default `pytest -q` pass. Scope is deliberately a small, hand-curated subset (currently one design), not every qualified artifact: only designs that (a) have a checked-in source .v under examples/designs/ and (b) are built by a plain `agamemnon build --uarch` (no --qualified-checkpoint route replay, which would make the 'route' constant by construction and defeat the point) are eligible. RE-BASELINING RULE: never update route_sha256 (or source_sha256) here just because the test failed. A mismatch means nextpnr's route for this exact source genuinely changed since the pin was set -- that is precisely the condition this file exists to surface. Before touching a pin: (1) determine whether the NEW route is a real regression or a real improvement/fix, (2) if it changes the emitted bitstream, re-verify on board (or, at minimum, record why board re-verification is not needed this time) exactly as qualification/pack_regression.json's own 'rebaselined' field requires for its goldens, (3) record a dated, specific 'reason' entry below citing that evidence. Re-baselining without independent re-verification is the exact process failure this mechanism exists to close.

designs.reason: Initial pin at T9/B3 closure. This is NOT a correctness certification of the pinned route -- it is reused verbatim from qualification/pack_regression.json's routed_sha256 for the board-verified 2026-08-02 checkpoint (qualification/mcu_ahb_constant_slave_routed.json), which IS independently board-verified (72/72 + 6/6 reads of 0x4147414d; see that file's own 'rebaselined' note and qualification/mcu_ahb_constant_slave_evidence.jsonl). A validation run on 2026-08-18 confirmed a genuine fresh `agamemnon build --uarch` of this exact source, on the current chipdb, does NOT reproduce this route (route sha256 7ace39b0b6bd82d93b263add9a944bf541b14fac5be1dde3d5db3fbd3cdef13a, 149 pips vs the checkpoint's 156) and packs to bitstream fc6919c2b1f76085cb9da217b85dc0d955e12ff3cf6e242bb5624d5487286909 -- the EXACT image that T22-T24 board-confirmed WRONG (reads 0x795fe3dd instead of 0x4147414d, 10/32 bits). This is expected and tracked, not a bug in this mechanism: it is the open, unresolved X14Y8 RMUX->IMUX->RMUX detour encoding defect (AG32-Docs docs/TASK_QUEUE.md queue B task B1). The corresponding test is marked xfail against exactly this reference; an unexpected XPASS is the signal that B1 has been fixed and this pin (and its xfail marker) should be reviewed. 2026-08-21 portability correction: source_sha256 now hashes canonical LF bytes, matching route-hash canonicalization and the committed Git blob; the prior d99acddb value was the same six-line source with CRLF working-tree endings. No source token or route pin changed.
